name: bbox-v1-core
title: bbox v1 core
description: The frozen v1 component set (packages/bbox-ui) as one module, `core.ts`, with its whole closure — what the v1 tldraw adapter imports. New work installs the trunk items instead.

files.content:
/**
 * packages/bbox-ui/src/codeField.fields.ts
 *
 * `CodeField`'s controllable props as data, so it can be a real member of
 * a real slot rather than something a parent composes for itself.
 *
 * WHY this file exists (Zach, 2026-09-15): Port's label slot became a
 * genuine slot — "even the text is just a member in the label slot that
 * can be deleted". A Port's label is "one line of code"
 * (`get_aruco: ArucoSrv`), so the member that carries it is the real
 * `CodeField`, not a plain TextBox: the monospace face, the grammar hook
 * and the caret behaviour ARE the thing being demonstrated.
 *
 * WHY the text field is `value` and not `children`, breaking step with
 * TextBox: a FieldSpec `id` must equal the real prop name it describes —
 * `readFields`/`toArgTypes` key off the string directly (see
 * `packages/schema/src/field.ts`). `CodeField` has no `children`; its text
 * has always been `value` (docs/TEXTBOX-EDITING-SPEC.md §1 draws the same
 * distinction from the other direction). Declaring `children` here to
 * match a sibling's spelling would put a control on screen that writes a
 * prop the component never reads.
 *
 * DELIBERATELY NARROW. `CodeFieldProps` carries ~25 props, most of them
 * host wiring (`onViewReady`, `tooltipParent`, `cursorAt`, `selectRange`,
 * the mode pair) that no author sets and a panel cannot meaningfully
 * offer. Only the fields below are things a person choosing how this field
 * LOOKS would reach for; the rest stay props for a host to drive.
 */
import type { FieldSpec } from "./schema";

export const CODE_FIELD_FIELDS: FieldSpec[] = [
  {
    id: "value",
    label: "Code",
    kind: "text",
    // CodeField is fully controlled — an empty string is its honest empty
    // state (a blank field showing `placeholder`), never a "fall through
    // to something else" sentinel.
    defaultValue: "",
    // Simple: this IS the field's content. Everything a person opens a
    // CodeField to change starts here (see `field.ts`'s `tier` docblock —
    // absent means Expert, Simple is hand-curated).
    tier: "simple",
  },
  {
    id: "placeholder",
    label: "Placeholder",
    kind: "text",
    defaultValue: "",
    hint: "Shown when Code is empty.",
  },
  {
    id: "align",
    label: "Align",
    kind: "segments",
    defaultValue: "left",
    options: [
      { value: "left", label: "Left" },
      { value: "right", label: "Right" },
    ],
    hint: "Which end the text hugs — a Port's label aligns toward its own dot.",
  },
  {
    id: "disabled",
    label: "Disabled",
    kind: "toggle",
    defaultValue: false,
    hint: "No caret, no edits — a read-only field.",
  },
];

/** No presets: `CodeField` has no governed paint ladder of its own — it
 *  inherits its font size from whatever wrapper it sits in (codeField.css
 *  reads it off the parent, see its own WHY), so there is nothing for a
 *  preset family to govern. */
export const CODE_FIELD_PRESETS = [];

/**
 * packages/bbox-ui/src/port.presets.ts
 *
 * `PORT_PRESETS` — one per `PortSizeRung` ("size", `port.fields.ts`'s own
 * cascading field), each a `size`-selected, mutually exclusive alternative
 * governing `diameter` and `textSize` together (Zach, 2026-09-11: "one
 * size rung, the same four names on every leaf" — a header hands its own
 * `size` down to its Ports, and one control should move both the dot and
 * its label instead of the two drifting independently). Port's colour is
 * still the hand-written `portDotStyle(state, tone)` lookup (./port.tsx)
 * this file's own earlier version described — that part is unaffected;
 * only the SIZE ladder now has a real governed set.
 *
 * Port's own diameter ladder tops out at "lg" (18px, `PORT_DIAMETERS`) —
 * it has no separate "xl" dot — so the "xl" size rung pairs that largest
 * real diameter with the largest text ("xl", 44px) rather than inventing
 * a fourth dot size nothing else on the board uses.
 */
import type { PresetSpec } from "./schema";

import {
  PORT_SIZE_RUNGS,
  PORT_SIZE_RUNG_LABELS,
  PORT_TEXT_LAYOUTS,
  PORT_TEXT_LAYOUT_LABELS,
  SECONDARY_LAYOUT_AS_ORIGIN,
  SECONDARY_SLOT_LAYOUTS,
  SECONDARY_SLOT_LAYOUT_LABELS,
  TEXT_LAYOUT_AS_PLACEMENT,
  type PortSizeRung,
} from "./port.layout";

const GOVERNS = ["diameter", "textSize"];

// WHY a total Record and not a ternary/lookup shortcut: a loose index
// signature would let a fifth rung typecheck clean and throw at render
// time reading `.diameter` off `undefined` — same defensive shape as
// pill.presets.ts's own PRESET_PAINT.
const PRESET_SIZE: Record<PortSizeRung, { diameter: string; textSize: string }> = {
  sm: { diameter: "sm", textSize: "sm" },
  md: { diameter: "md", textSize: "md" },
  lg: { diameter: "lg", textSize: "lg" },
  // Port has no "xl" diameter of its own — 18px ("lg") stays its largest
  // dot, so the "xl" rung pairs that ceiling diameter with "xl" text.
  xl: { diameter: "lg", textSize: "xl" },
};

export const PORT_PRESETS: PresetSpec[] = PORT_SIZE_RUNGS.map((size) => ({
  id: size,
  label: PORT_SIZE_RUNG_LABELS[size],
  selector: "size",
  governs: GOVERNS,
  values: PRESET_SIZE[size],
}));

/**
 * The two SLOT-PLACEMENT ladders — `textLayout` governing the label slot's
 * placement fields, `secondarySlotLayout` governing the secondary slot's.
 *
 * WHY these exist at all, when `LabeledPort` already resolves the same
 * thing with `labelOrigin ?? TEXT_LAYOUT_AS_PLACEMENT[layout].origin`:
 * because a runtime `??` is invisible to the SCHEMA layer, and the schema
 * layer is what decides whether a field gets materialised as an explicit
 * value. `defaultArgs` omits governed fields precisely so a selector can
 * still select (see its own WHY) — but it can only omit what a
 * `PresetSpec` declares. Left undeclared, every placement field shipped
 * its default as an explicit arg that outranked the preset, which is how
 * `labelOffsetY` came to pin a plain `right` label 23px high (2026-09-15).
 *
 * WHY a projection of `TEXT_LAYOUT_AS_PLACEMENT` rather than its own
 * table: so the ladder the component renders from and the ladder the
 * inspector reasons about cannot drift. There is still exactly ONE table
 * of placements in this repo; this is a second VIEW of it, and
 * `port.fields.test.ts` asserts the view still matches the component's
 * own fallback chain for every member.
 *
 * `labelOffsetX`, `secondaryAlign` and both secondary offsets stay
 * UNGOVERNED on purpose: they take the same static value on every rung,
 * so they have a real default rather than a preset-varying one, and
 * materialising them changes nothing.
 */
export const LABEL_PLACEMENT_PRESETS: PresetSpec[] = PORT_TEXT_LAYOUTS.map((layout) => ({
  id: layout,
  label: PORT_TEXT_LAYOUT_LABELS[layout],
  selector: "textLayout",
  governs: ["labelOrigin", "labelAlign", "labelOffsetY"],
  values: {
    labelOrigin: TEXT_LAYOUT_AS_PLACEMENT[layout].origin,
    labelAlign: TEXT_LAYOUT_AS_PLACEMENT[layout].align,
    labelOffsetY: TEXT_LAYOUT_AS_PLACEMENT[layout].offsetY,
  },
}));

export const SECONDARY_PLACEMENT_PRESETS: PresetSpec[] = SECONDARY_SLOT_LAYOUTS.map((layout) => ({
  id: layout,
  label: SECONDARY_SLOT_LAYOUT_LABELS[layout],
  selector: "secondarySlotLayout",
  governs: ["secondaryOrigin"],
  values: { secondaryOrigin: SECONDARY_LAYOUT_AS_ORIGIN[layout] },
}));

/**
 * Every preset a `LabeledPort` answers to — the array `defaultArgs` and
 * any inspector must be handed, since each selector governs a DISJOINT
 * set (`assertDisjointPresets` proves it in the tests).
 *
 * `PORT_PRESETS` stays the size ladder alone: it is what a bare `Port`
 * (geometry only, no slots) resolves `diameter` through, and that
 * primitive has no placement fields to govern.
 */
export const LABELED_PORT_PRESETS: PresetSpec[] = [
  ...PORT_PRESETS,
  ...LABEL_PLACEMENT_PRESETS,
  ...SECONDARY_PLACEMENT_PRESETS,
];

/**
 * packages/bbox-ui/src/region.presets.ts
 *
 * `REGION_PRESETS` is deliberately empty: a Region has NO `view` selector
 * — it is not collapsible the way `Block` now is (`block.presets.ts`).
 * Instead it composes a real `Block` (in Port view) into its corner —
 * the 2026-09-11 report's own C7 ruling, Zach's words: "a region is not a
 * block but is composed using a block." Kept as a real, empty, exported
 * array (`block.presets.ts`'s own precedent) rather than omitted, so a
 * generic story generator / product inspector can always `.map()` over
 * `<NAME>_PRESETS` without a null check.
 */
import type { PresetSpec } from "./schema";

export const REGION_PRESETS: PresetSpec[] = [];

/**
 * bbox-ui skin — the SHAPE language, the third orthogonal appearance axis.
 *
 * WHY a third axis beside theme.css and appearance.ts, rather than more
 * rungs on either: the three answer different questions and compose
 * freely.
 *
 *   theme      (theme.css, `data-theme`)  — WHICH COLOURS. light / dark.
 *   appearance (appearance.ts, `state`)   — WHAT THIS THING IS. empty /
 *                                           valueSet / wired / received.
 *   skin       (this file, `data-bbox-skin`) — WHAT IT IS DRAWN LIKE.
 *                                           default / plain / sketch.
 *
 * A sketch-skinned board in dark mode with a wired Port is all three at
 * once, and no axis knows the others exist. Folding skin into `state`'s
 * preset family would have made them a single 3 x 2 x 4 enum and broken
 * `assertDisjointPresets` the moment two selectors both claimed
 * `lineColor` — see the module doc in `appearance.ts` on why `tone` is an
 * override rather than a second preset family, which is the same argument.
 *
 * WHY a CSS custom-property layer and not a prop, a preset family or a
 * cva variant (the three alternatives scored in
 * reports/component-skins-proposal-2026-09-17.html):
 *
 *   - It is INHERITED, so one attribute on any ancestor re-skins an entire
 *     board. A prop would have to be threaded through every component,
 *     every adapter and every shape record.
 *   - It costs the adapters NOTHING. A tldraw shape and a React Flow node
 *     are DOM inside a container the host already owns, so both inherit a
 *     skin with zero adapter edits — verified in demos/tldraw and
 *     demos/reactflow, neither of which changed a component call.
 *   - It stays OUT of the document. A skin is a view preference like
 *     light/dark, not a fact about the system being drawn. Modelling it as
 *     a field would persist it into every saved board.
 *   - `shadcn add` is untouched: skins are one optional stylesheet, not a
 *     per-component file that has to land as a sibling.
 *
 * The cost this buys, stated plainly: a skin does NOT appear in a
 * `FieldTrace`, so the inspector cannot say "the sketch skin supplied this
 * radius" the way it says "the wired preset supplied this colour". See the
 * report's "what this gives up" section.
 *
 * INVARIANT — a skin never moves anything. Every token below paints; none
 * of them is a length that layout.ts / blockLayout.ts / portPlacement.ts
 * reads. That is what makes a skin safe to switch under a live canvas:
 * port anchors, edge endpoints and hit-test boxes are byte-identical
 * across all three. `demos/capture-skins.mjs` measures the spatial half in
 * a real browser (every port-dot centre, both hosts); `test/skin.test.ts`
 * holds the half that can fail in CI — no skin varies the stroke width, no
 * skin introduces a transform. It is also why
 * there is deliberately no `rotate` token, tempting as one is for sketch:
 * rotating the DOM would desynchronise it from the host's own geometry,
 * which the core does not own (see CLAUDE.md's one rule).
 */

/**
 * WHY the array is the source and the type is derived: the same rule
 * `TEXT_BOX_FONTS` and `BLOCK_ORIENTATIONS` already follow here — a
 * hand-written union lets the vocabulary and the thing that renders it
 * drift, and every total `Record<Skin, …>` below becomes a compile error
 * until a new skin says what it paints.
 */
export const BBOX_SKINS = ["default", "plain", "sketch"] as const;
export type BboxSkin = (typeof BBOX_SKINS)[number];

export const BBOX_SKIN_LABELS: Record<BboxSkin, string> = {
  default: "Default",
  plain: "Plain",
  sketch: "Sketch",
};

export const BBOX_SKIN_BLURBS: Record<BboxSkin, string> = {
  default: "Today's wireframe: 2px foreground outline, 8px corners. Unchanged, and what you get when no skin is set.",
  plain: "Square corners, one hairline, no shadow. The austere reading — Base UI's docs, a schematic.",
  sketch: "Hand-drawn: an informal font and corners that are not quite the same on any two sides.",
};

/**
 * The attribute a host stamps. Any ancestor will do — `<html>` for a whole
 * app, a single `<Block>` for one card — because every token below
 * inherits.
 *
 * WHY an attribute and not a class: it is single-valued. A class set
 * (`skin-sketch skin-plain`) can hold two skins at once and the cascade
 * picks by source order, which is a bug you cannot see in the DOM. An
 * attribute makes "exactly one skin is active here" structural.
 */
export const BBOX_SKIN_ATTR = "data-bbox-skin";

/**
 * The closed token set a skin may define — real exported data, not a
 * comment, so `test/skin.test.ts` can assert that `skin.css` defines exactly
 * these for exactly the skins in `BBOX_SKINS` and no others, and that each
 * component's own `var()` fallback still matches what is advertised here. A
 * token that exists in the CSS but not here (or vice versa) is the
 * failure this list is here to catch: it renders as "the default" and
 * looks like a design decision rather than a typo.
 *
 * Each entry carries the fallback the COMPONENT hard-codes at its call
 * site, which is today's look. That is what makes `skin.css` optional: a
 * consumer who never imports it sees the pixels they have now.
 */
export interface SkinToken {
  /** Custom property name, without the leading `--`. */
  name: string;
  /**
   * What the component falls back to when no skin stylesheet is loaded —
   * the literal text after the comma in its `var()`.
   *
   * `null` means the fallback is COMPUTED by the component's own cascade
   * rather than written in the source: `--bbox-skin-line-override` falls
   * back to whatever colour `resolveField` produced for that instance, and
   * `--bbox-skin-dot-rings` to a box-shadow layer list built at render
   * time. That is not a gap in this table, it is the distinction the table
   * exists to record — a `null` here marks a token the skin is allowed to
   * SUPPRESS but never to colour, because the colour belongs to the
   * `state` preset family and two selectors owning one field is what
   * `assertDisjointPresets` forbids.
   */
  fallback: string | null;
  /** Which CSS property it ends up in, for the docs table. */
  paints: string;
}

export const BBOX_SKIN_TOKENS: readonly SkinToken[] = [
  { name: "bbox-skin-radius", fallback: "8px", paints: "border-radius (Block, Region)" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-radius-pill", fallback: "9999px", paints: "border-radius (Pill, BlockChip)" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-stroke-width", fallback: "2px", paints: "border-width" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-stroke", fallback: "var(--color-foreground)", paints: "border-color" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-surface", fallback: "var(--color-card)", paints: "background" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-shadow", fallback: "none", paints: "box-shadow" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-font", fallback: "inherit", paints: "font-family (inherited by every text slot)" },
  // The two that switch between a CSS border and a drawn one. `outline` is
  // a `display` value, not a colour: only the sketch skin sets it to
  // `block`, so every other skin renders `SketchOutline` and never paints
  // it. See sketchOutline.tsx on why it cannot be conditional in React.
  { name: "bbox-skin-outline", fallback: "none", paints: "display (SketchOutline's <svg>)" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-ink", fallback: "var(--color-foreground)", paints: "stroke (the drawn line)" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-fg", fallback: "var(--color-card-foreground)", paints: "color (Block's text, which a fill-less skin must re-point)" },
  // Lets a skin blank out a border whose COLOUR belongs to another axis.
  // Pill, Bar and Port paint their line from the `state` preset family, so
  // the skin may not name a colour for them — but it may say "do not paint
  // the CSS one, the drawn one is taking its place". Undefined on every
  // skin but sketch, so the `var()` fallback is the real colour.
  { name: "bbox-skin-line-override", fallback: null, paints: "border-color on state-painted components (Pill, Bar)" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-font-sans", fallback: 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif', paints: "font-family for a TextBox's `sans` rung, which is set inline and so beats inheritance" },
  { name: "bbox-skin-font-mono", fallback: 'ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace', paints: "font-family inside a CodeField and a TextBox's `mono` rung" },
  // The inverse of `--bbox-skin-outline`, for the one case where a skin
  // cannot recolour the crisp version away: an SVG path has no
  // "transparent but still there" the way a border does, and a Trace's `d`
  // is computed by the HOST, so the component renders both the crisp path
  // and the drawn one and CSS picks. Paths do not affect layout, so the
  // hidden one costs nothing but the memoised math.
  { name: "bbox-skin-crisp", fallback: "inline", paints: "display (the un-sketched twin of a drawn element)" },
  // A Port's rings are box-shadow layers, not a border, so `transparent`
  // is not a way to blank them. Same contract as line-override: the skin
  // names no colour, only "do not paint the CSS one".
  { name: "bbox-skin-dot-rings", fallback: null, paints: "box-shadow (a Port dot's state rings)" },
] as const;

/**
 * `{ "data-bbox-skin": skin }`, ready to spread onto any element.
 *
 * WHY a helper for one key: the attribute name is the whole public
 * contract between this package and a host's CSS, and a host that types
 * `data-bbox-theme` by hand gets no error — just a board that never
 * changes. One import, one typo-proof spelling, and `BboxSkin` narrows
 * the value.
 */
export function bboxSkinAttrs(skin: BboxSkin): Record<string, string> {
  return { [BBOX_SKIN_ATTR]: skin };
}
